project.researchNotes: Full current-web audit. All six visitor categories and four named clue-trail providers checked. Inverurie attractions and services were excluded. The single HES listed building is present, materially dated and named without appended date text.

touristAppeal.label: Limited Interest
touristAppeal.summary: A pleasant 2.8 km canal-and-riverside circuit with surviving transport heritage and good open-space links, but no verified café, formal picnic site, dependable visitor car park or public toilet inside the settlement.
touristAppeal.dogAccessSummary: The outdoor circuit can suit responsible dog walking, with close control beside water, roads, wildlife and other users.

townGuide.headline: A worthwhile short circuit, not a complete visitor town
townGuide.intro: Port Elphinstone scores 54% after a full second pass. The canal remains, listed sluices and official 2.8 km loop justify a focused short stop, but Inverurie’s museum, cafés and practical facilities cannot be borrowed.

suggestedFirstVisit.title: Use the official 2.8 km route
suggestedFirstVisit.summary: Follow the mapped circuit through the settlement and canal-side green network.

townGuide.visitorMood: Green and locally interesting, with limited visitor infrastructure.

features.name: Aberdeenshire Canal Remains and Sluice Bridges
features.shortDescription: The surviving terminus-side canal channel and listed 1796 sluice bridges, interpreted on the council’s mapped local walk.

attractionGuide.headline: Follow the surviving end of the Aberdeen–Inverurie canal
attractionGuide.intro: Port Elphinstone preserves canal fabric and a waterside path from the transport scheme that gave the settlement its name.
attractionGuide.parking: Davidson Park is evidenced as an open space and recycling location, but no dependable public visitor-car-park specification was found.
attractionGuide.toilets: No public toilet was verified inside Port Elphinstone.
attractionGuide.picnic: No formal picnic tables or dedicated picnic site were verified.
